html:
After the American War of Independence, thousands of Loyalists who had sided with Britain fled to the Bahamas from 1783, many from Georgia and the Carolinas. They brought enslaved Africans with them.

The newcomers more than doubled the population and made Black people the majority. They set up cotton plantations on the outer islands, but the thin soil and insects ruined the crop within a generation.

Many planters left, and the enslaved people they abandoned worked the land on their own. Their descendants form most of the people of the Bahamas today. Other Loyalists went north, as told under Loyalists to Canada, and to Jamaica.
sum: After the American War of Independence, thousands of Loyalists who had sided with Britain fled to the Bahamas from 1783, many from Georgia and the Carolinas. They brought enslaved Africans with them.
